newsitem.title: USA: IPO SPOTLIGHT-Cellnet seen up over offer.
newsitem.headline: IPO SPOTLIGHT-Cellnet seen up over offer.

text.p: Wireless network system operator Cellnet Data Systems, one of the new issues to hit the street this week, is expected to trade at least two points over its offering price on the strength of the reputation of its lead underwriter, analysts said.
The analysts, who follow the initial offering market, said said the IPO had the advantage of being sponsored by an underwriting group led by Morgan Stanley.
"I am enthused about the underwriting group that has been put together for the stock," said David Menlow, president of IPO Financial Network Corp based in Springfield, N.J.
Cellnet builds and operates wireless networks. It is expected to offer five million shares by Friday at between $19 and $21 under the proposed symbol CNDS.O on the Nasdaq National Market.
Analyst Steven Tuen of IPO Value Monitor was less optimistic about the company's future, citing its plans to build its wireless networks and infrastructure as a drag on earnings.
"We're not too crazy about it. We doubt the company will report earnings until 1999. It will spend a lot of money to build up their infrastructure," Tuen said.

Tuen, like Menlow, did note lead underwriter Morgan Stanley's involvement in the deal as an important factor in boosting the company's profile based on Morgan's strong track record with its offerings.
Cellnet's 1995 revenues rose to $2.126 million from $1.651 million the previous year but 1995 net losses increased to $40.956 million from $14.634 million in 1994.
